Audience: first-time Hawaii class three applicants, including minors on the graduated path, learning downshifting limits, parking placement, parking on a hill, angle and parallel parking, parking restrictions, electric and hand signals, hazard and stop signals, turn signal rules and errors, sharing the road with vehicles of all sizes, and driving in rain, hydroplaning, wet brakes, floods, fog and winter conditions in plain English.

Prerequisites: the brake and downshifting material that opens this section continues from the previous section, and the signal law of the traffic laws section is restated here in practice.

Scope note: downshifting limits and cautions, parking placement, parking on a hill, angle and parallel parking, parking restrictions, electric and hand signals with their advantages and disadvantages, hazard and stop signals, the rules and common errors of turn signals, the traffic mix, and inclement weather including rain, oil film, hydroplaning, wet brakes, floods, fog and winter conditions. Freeway and emergency driving follow in the next section.

Recall emphasis: the hydroplaning speeds, the fog stopping distance, the parking distances and the signal law are practiced as recall items; no scenario or recognition surface is needed for this section.
